BLOCKER: Gate decisions are plain JSON fields in the item; nothing enforces "recorded only by the HIL session" — any agent/script can write {gate, decision, by, findings_sha, at} and self-approve, defeating fail-closed and never-auto-approved claims.

`by` is asserted and `at` client-supplied (SSO out-of-scope), so both the ordering predicate (decision.at >= evidence.at) and human-approval proof are forgeable; STALE_APPROVAL is not a real integrity control.

set_status/gate1 enforcement is only at precheck/CI on the committed diff; in-process library/epic-rollup transitions have no gate1 predicate (only gate2_ready named), leaving a control-plane bypass window between runs.
MAJOR: Rollback is only "Revert the change": no handling for decision records/baseline entries already appended, or for items left blocked after revert; checklist guardrail 1/6 not actually answered.
No stated defence-in-depth or alerting: baseline expiry flips entries to DENY with no lead-time alert, and no metric/log is specified for DENY/override rates (checklist 2 and 10 unanswered).

Force override auditability is not closed: PF_GATE_FORCE run appends a gate_override record, but nothing guarantees the local run commits it before the bypass takes effect; PF_CI-unset check is trivially defeated by shell env.
Design-sha covers mutable body fields (components/files/risks/rollback) but the design does not pin canonical serialization/ordering of the hashed fields, risking sha mismatch across edits/reformats.
Design does not explicitly answer checklist items 3/9/RLS scope beyond a one-line "control-plane, non-tenant"; no test asserts decision records are excluded from tenant queries.
MINOR: CL-001 single-writer question unresolved: decisions flow through core.backlog.update while status flows through set_status — two write paths for one aggregate with no stated ownership arbitration.
--report exit-0 mode has no stated guard against being used as the pass signal in scripts (reason codes printed but no machine-readable schema/version specified).
Baseline entries edited in the same PR that expires them are "ordinary reviewed changes" with no conflict-of-interest or independent-approver rule.
No positive-path self-test listed (only allow + deny x5), so a checker that always DENYs could pass the negative suite.
NIT: diff_sha[:12]/design_sha[:12] truncation collisions are theoretical but worth a documented full-sha reference alongside the short form.
Language-rule rationale is recorded only in the item; a pointer in docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md would prevent re-litigation.
SUMMARY: Verdict: predicate reuse and fail-closed intent are sound, but the gate's trust anchor is convention, not enforcement — decisions and timestamps are forgeable, so Gate 1/2 can be self-satisfied despite the schema.

Top risks: (1) HIL-only decision writes are unenforced, (2) forgeable `by`/`at` invalidates the ordering predicate, (3) rollback/observability guardrails from the checklist are not actually answered in the design.
Address the trust boundary (write-path enforcement or cryptographic/CI-verified attestation) before Gate 1 approval.
